ideas.title: Three bells, three notes
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: This is the third 'knock it and hear its solved modes' film in a row: three struck objects with a mode shimmer is the lantern post's recipe with bronze. The one real step is that the shape is cut by hand and changes the note, and the pitch only delivers that if the player does the cutting, not if Lumi does it offscreen.

ideas.title: Damp sand stands, dry sand pours
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A GPU grain sim with cohesion that fades as the sand dries is physics the island has never had, and cohesion that reads at a glance is a hard, honest test. The three tunnels are a demo setup, and digging sand is only loosely tied to making things that keep their marks.

ideas.title: Glass held and blown
ideas.critique: This is a retake of the glass film, with the earlier critic's notes turned into the pitch, so anyone who knows the island has seen this bubble twice. Lumi's wing really driving the pipe and true transmissive cooling glass would be real fixes, but they make the glass work, not a new thing.

ideas.title: The lathe cuts a top
ideas.critique: Cutting the profile with the mouse and then watching that exact mass distribution flip or not on the board is a loop players will repeat. The top solver already exists, so the risk is that the mouse-carving feels like dragging a spline rather than a chisel biting into spinning wood.

ideas.title: The kick wheel in Jump in
ideas.critique: This is the core of the big goal made playable: throw, cut, fire, and see glaze pool in your own cuts. Everyone expects it after the jar, though, and a profile that follows the mouse is a lathe curve, not clay pushed under fingers.

ideas.title: Paint that stays on my feathers
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Paint that stays where it hit is the human's own spray-can example, so it is predictable even on creature skin. Flaking at the joints that move most and washing out only where pond water runs over it are the parts that would make it more than a texture stamp.

ideas.title: A real fall
ideas.critique: An active ragdoll with motors and a balance controller is a real engineered system the island lacks, and it serves the animation goal directly. Three falls in a film is little to play with, and it has almost nothing to do with things made by hand.

ideas.title: A letter that flutters
same_form: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A sheet falling has been filmed twice and missed twice. A pitching moment and stiff creases is the mechanism those posts lacked, so it counts only if different folds clearly give different flights. Otherwise it is a third drifting page.

ideas.title: Flint that cuts
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Linking materials, so a knapped edge becomes a tool that works on clay and wood, is exactly what the big goal asks for. But 'sharpness measured from the mesh' can easily collapse into a threshold that switches cutting on, and the knapping itself has been seen.

ideas.title: One stone in the surf
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Shallow water with sediment transport on the GPU is new physics, and scour or a tongue of sand behind an obstacle is a real, recognisable effect. Placing one stone and watching is a toy you look at once, and it serves the sea candidate, not the workshop goal.
